title: German engineering group posts higher first-half profit, raises outlook
text: A German industrial engineering group on Tuesday reported a 12 percent rise in first-half operating profit, citing strong demand for its turbine components in Asia. The company raised its full-year earnings forecast and said order books were at their highest level in five years. Analysts said the results beat consensus expectations and several brokerages lifted their price targets.

title: Sterling firms against dollar as rate expectations shift
text: Sterling rose against the dollar in early European trading on Thursday as dealers priced in a growing likelihood of a rise in British interest rates before year-end. The pound touched a three-month high before easing back slightly. Money market rates also edged higher, while gilts were little changed in thin trade.

title: Copper prices climb on supply worries after mine strike vote
text: Copper futures rose more than two percent on Wednesday after workers at one of the world's largest copper mines voted to authorize a strike over pay. Traders said the threat of a prolonged stoppage could tighten an already thin spot market. Other base metals were mixed, with aluminium ending slightly lower.

title: Consumer prices rise 0.3 percent as fuel costs jump
text: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent last month, the government said on Friday, as a jump in fuel costs offset flat food prices. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the index rose 0.2 percent. Economists said the figures were unlikely to change the central bank's cautious stance on monetary policy.

title: French utility agrees to buy rival's water business for $2.1 billion
text: A French utility said on Monday it had agreed to acquire the water treatment business of a domestic rival for $2.1 billion in cash, its largest purchase in a decade. The deal, which requires regulatory approval, would make the company the second-largest water services provider in Europe. The seller said it would use the proceeds to cut debt.

title: Typhoon lashes northern Philippines, thousands evacuated
text: A powerful typhoon swept across the northern Philippines on Sunday, toppling power lines and forcing more than 30,000 people from their homes, disaster officials said. Two fishermen were reported missing and several coastal towns were flooded. Forecasters said the storm was expected to weaken as it moved into the South China Sea.

title: EU ministers fail to agree on fishing quota reform
text: European Union fisheries ministers ended two days of talks on Tuesday without agreement on proposed cuts to North Sea fishing quotas, diplomats said. Southern member states opposed the reductions, arguing they would devastate coastal communities. Officials said negotiations would resume next month under the incoming presidency.

title: Ceasefire talks resume as fighting flares in border region
text: Negotiators from two warring factions resumed ceasefire talks in Nairobi on Wednesday, even as fresh fighting was reported near the disputed border region. Aid agencies said renewed shelling had cut off relief convoys to three towns. Mediators said they remained hopeful a framework agreement could be signed within weeks.

title: Japan posts wider trade surplus as exports surge
text: Japan's trade surplus widened for the fourth straight month in June as exports of vehicles and electronics surged, finance ministry data showed on Thursday. The surplus rose 18 percent from a year earlier. Economists warned the widening gap could renew trade friction with the United States, while a weaker yen continued to support exporters.

title: Drugmaker names new chief executive, shares rise
text: A U.S. pharmaceutical company said on Monday its board had appointed the head of its research division as chief executive, succeeding the retiring incumbent at the end of the year. The shares rose three percent on the announcement. The incoming chief said the company would focus on its late-stage pipeline and consider selective acquisitions.
